HOWEVER, I immediately noticed that this item did not include a blue light testing light and card, which sort of made me suspicious as I've previously ordered other anti-blue light glasses that include the light and card. I took the blue light blocking light and card from another pair I'd previously ordered, and tested them on this set of glasses. I could instantly tell that the glasses were not blocking blue light, as the light was able to penetrate the lenses and mark the card. On 2-3 other pairs of glasses that were all advertised as blue light blockers, I tested them and the light did not mark the card.

This listing and label in the clothing says that it is 93% cotton and 7% spandex. That is just not what this feels and looks like. Yes, it has cotton in it. That I can see. However, this fleece lining is not cotton. I have had cotton fleece lined fabrics many times. They do NOT feel like this. I have two photos for you with this listing. One shows the hem which has outside and inside in one picture. The other is the fleece inside.

COLOR
The color of this is a pretty nice cranberry red.

FIT
This set fits well. It is an XL and I usually wear a size 14=16 misses US size. This fits very well and is not at all tight or restrictive.

PERFORMANCE
I prefer all cotton long underwear. I feel that whatever this is fleeced with is synthetic and I am not as fond of it. If it is very cold out, I will wear this, but I am not as happy as if it was all cotton as that breathes better.

STRETCH
This set stretches very nicely and gives well.

THE BOTTOM LINE
If this set was all cotton as ilsted I would be crazy about it. As it is, I will use it, but not as much as otherwise. It fits well, and stretches nicely so I am happy with that part. The color is a nice cranberry red too.

MY RATING
THREE STARS. I was expecting cotton and this just is not what I was expecting. I still will wear it and use it, but I would have liked it if the description was more accurate. If synthetics do not bother you and you love wearing them, then you will probably love this set.

All of his shoes show a size 10 US and size 43 EU, but these were marked 45 EU and 10 US. So the manufacture does not have the accurate sizing on the shoes. So beware when ordering the sizes because they are not true US sizing.

제목: Quite a Feat to Put On At First But It Gets Easier After Awhile
본문:
This review is for Shape Concept 067 Fajas Colombianas para Hombres Mens Girdle High Compression Garmen Shapewear Body Shaper for Men (Cocoa). I'm 5'7" (1.7m) with 32" (82cm) waist and pretty fit. I got this body shaper in the Large size because of the reviews saying it was extremely small. While this may be true at first, I think I might have been better off getting the Medium, as per the product specifications. It's meant to be worn very tight against the body and it defeats the purpose if it's too loose. The large size is OK still for me, but I feel the Medium would probably help me much more to firm up my abs. I should have trusted the manufacturer to give the proper sizing for my body in this case. If I were to buy again, I would trust the manufacturer's recommended size and go with the Medium. I think we just have to get used to the tight fit and let the compression suit do what it's designed to do. It may be a struggle at first but over time it gets much easier so in that sense, I think it was sized properly for a fit body type.
Despite getting a size Large, the first time I put this on, it was a feat in itself! It was rather difficult to put my arms through the suit once I had my legs firmly placed inside. It was then really hard to zip up but I managed. It was almost hard to breathe with it on too at first, but after a bit of getting used to the compression, I thought it was fine. Taking it off is much easier. I washed and dried it as per instructions (handwash cycle only) and I found the next few times I put it on, it was much much easier. I'm was hoping this compression suit would help me with my back pain somewhat after working out in the yard and doing lots of heavy lifting. It's too soon to say for now but I feel like it does help keep my back more aligned. I thought the material was very breathable (84% nylon and 16% spandex). I was not sweating in it as I had feared could happen with some compression suits so that was a relief. I will probably not be able to wear it as often in the warmer months though because it's another layer of clothing that will just heat me up despite the breathability. I plan on wearing it more in the winter time when it would not be too obvious that I am wearing a body suit. The cocoa color seems appropriate for me because I get extremely tanned during the summer but it's still obvious that I am wearing it when the sleeves poke out from under my t-shirt. The wide neck is great and it doesn't show but the sleeves are a little long for me. Overall, after wearing this for almost 2 weeks on and off, I thought it was a nice compression body suit for people who are fairly fit and healthy. If you are somewhat overweight or top heavy, I seriously doubt that you can fit into the suit though, but that's just a guess. You will definitely be struggling to put it on, and that's not a guess. If you are fit and healthy, I would recommend this body suit and go as tight as you can so you will benefit from it more. I'd give it a 4.2/5.0 - 08/16/2022

I bought this as an alternative to a $300 new hunting saddle. I'm 6'4", 225lbs, 35" waist 34" inseam for what its worth. I have owned several different black diamond harnesses over the years for climbing and rappelling, and have what I would consider a novice level of climbing ability. I would have never bought this harness for climbing rock. 20' up a tree to me is a lot different than 100'+ up a rock. That said, I wouldn't hesitate to use this for rock climbing. It may not be a Petzl, but you can't expect that for this kind of money. I would put this unit on par or better than most of the average entry level climbing harnesses on the market. I will only be using this for tree climbing, and perhaps some roofing this coming summer when I re-shingle my main peak on my house, but the quality on the SUB harness is pretty darn tight.

Now, for fit: I gave my weight/dims above. This harness is tight on me. Any more than a 36" waist and you're going to want something more than a one size adult harness. That said, I can get into it with my hunting gear on, and its quiet in the woods (I did tape up the rear buckle to keep it from clanging without a strap in it). My clydesdale legs fit just fine with lots of room to spare in the thighs, and the saddle/support is a good fit. The reviews about the tightness when tied in are warranted, but honestly, if I can find this comfy while dangling from a tree trying not to fall asleep at 0530 on a 32* morning waiting for bambi's uncle to start sniffing my scrape, I can't imagine why anyone really should complain about it.

For the hunter's out there, I combined this with a HSS lifeline and a Muddy tether. I don't carry a foot stand, yet (still debating on that). This combo with a 50' length of 550 cord is extremely mobile, and the weight is not noticeable, especially if you carry a backpack. I can't say its quite as comfortable as falling asleep in my tree stand, but its darn close.

The most stand-out feature of these shorts is the lack of standout features on these shorts. Everything seems to fall somewhere between barely-acceptable and good-enough. I use these for gravel and bike touring anywhere from 30 to 90 miles at a stretch (2-8 hours in the saddle), and the best I can say about them is "meh."

If anything, they run a tiny bit (half size) small. The material is durable, but a little on the harsh side (once I got a sunburn while riding, and the shorts actually abraded off the top layers of skin, leading to a pretty bad wound). The zipper pockets are just barely big enough to hold a Samsung Galaxy A11 smart phone WITHOUT a case. If you have a bigger phone or a bulky case on yours, forget it. Wallet and a car key, sure. Don't even think of putting anything valuable or important in the side pockets. They are shallow and stuff is going to fall out. Those are for holding a couple Clif bars at best.

The length is so-so. The liner on these things seems to sit a little low, so to get the chamois properly positioned betwixt your nethers you'll need to pull these up past your belly button and snug down the draw string, and then the legs seem to only come down to mid-thigh (admittedly, I am a pretty tall guy around 6'3"). I have pretty big quadriceps from biking, and while these shorts fit, they are a little snug.

All that being said, they work-ish. My rear is usually ok-enough to keep pedaling at the tail end of a long ride. They have held up to lots of washes, they look normal enough that you won't draw unwanted attention if you stop in a gas station to buy snacks or drink. For the casual rider who is just getting started, they will work and not break the bank. I just can't give these a great review because there are much better options around the same price point (check out Baleaf cycling shorts if you are on a budget - much better chamois). They aren't that comfortable. The padding is barely serviceable. The pockets are a little too small. The legs are a little too short. The liner sits a bit too low.

I skied a 5 hour day and used the gloves intermittently throughout the day as to not sweat. I would turn the gloves on, warm my hands, turn them off. The first time I used them, I did so without liners. That was a terrible idea. The material in these gloves absorbs moisture. GET LINERS. As a watch enthusiast and collector, I'll own up to spending far more time than might be sensible scrolling and searching Amazon for bargains or interesting time pieces. It seems regardless of the focus of my searches, brands like OLEVS and OUPINKE (or OPK, TDO and JSDun ) tend to pop up in all the time with any number of representations of their "luxurious attributes." I decided to pick up a few samples from the aforementioned brands - which appear to be mushroom varieties from the same manufacturer - to see for myself how well they hold up to the promotional come-ons.

The accompanying photo reflects two watches from this manufacturer's stable: the blue sunburst dial styled OPK and a similarly styled OLEVS model. While the two minimalist watches have modest differences in hand styles, dial markers and different disappointing stainless steel bracelets, in terms of overall look and functionality, they're essentially consecutive slices of white bread. In each instance here, the hands and dotted markers are lumed although the longevity of illumination is less than sufficient. If anything, the lighter weight OPK (69g) with the beads of rice plated band might be the least adequate of the six or so watches I acquired from this company for comparison purposes. The coated mesh bracelet employs a rattling stamped folding deployant clasp with two button release. For reasons that can only be speculated, this watch (as well as associated models from this concern) are shipped without crown retainers so it's a coin toss whether they'll be received with dead batteries or minimally, batteries that will have an inordinately reduced life span. All the these watches have snap off/on pressure closure stainless steel back case covers that is basically a consistent indicator of low end yet from the half full glass perspective, not much of an issue to replace if you have the appropriate cover replacement gadget.

From a cursory glance many of these inexpensive models from each label seem relatively attractive and in numerable instances the only pertinent differences are the logos on the packaging and watch dials. On closer examination - let alone under magnification - most simply fail to pass muster even with consideration of the relatively low price point. A few do not seem to be horrible and a waste of money at any price point and some potential purchasers may even consider these generally modest overall quality watches a good value. While all of them seem to employ arguably accurate lower end Japanese quartz movements which I suppose is the primary objective, nearly all of the quartz movement models I've acquired with a day/date complication are mired with misalignment issues in the date window. That said, I tend to believe these watches are of comparable quality to a host of popular designer branded watches employing effectively the same quality of materials but carrying substantially inflated retail prices.

I cannot speak to how prevalent that deficiency is with the automatics or any of the models with the faux jewel dials and bezels because they are simply too gaudy for me to even have in my possession.Generally, there doesn't seem to be a major amount of differentiation between the OLEVS, OUPINKE, TDO or JSDun watches. No matter which branding you decide on it's probably a good idea just to avoid any of the purported stainless steel bracelets and opt for the arguably decent quality leather bands. While top surfaces of the links on the silver stainless steel bracelets are shiny and glimmering, I haven't found a single instance where the underside was commensurably finished. With the majority, the link end caps look dull not in the manner of a brushed finish but rather as though they were not buffed at all.

However, if you do decide to be the intrepid explorer with the stainless steel, the ion plated or coated models seem to be of higher aesthetic quality the polished stainless steel. At least the coating tends to obviate some of the rattling...excluding the beads of rice models. Just don't go there at all. Similarly the black or antiqued gold tone cases are a less off-putting choice than the yellow gold tone or the silver cases which tend to appear plated substitutions for the actual metals or minerals. The stainless steel cases might be a tolerable choice so long as it is not paired with one of the mediocre polished stainless steel bracelets where the end result is a watch that just shimmers CHEAP.

Ok. So I ordered this while overseas and had it shipped. By the time I got to test it in a rain, the return window had passed but that's not the issue, though I would have sent it back and gotten a refund if I'd been in the states!

1) Ladies....this thing is hot. I suppose it's ok if you're standing still or there's a breeze, but if you live in someplace like Florida, or a similar humid and hot region like Tokyo, this thing is going to make you uncomfortably sweaty. I know they say it breathes, but the only air that got into this thing was when my 5 year old grabbed onto the back of it and tried to make it flap like a superhero's cape. Since that was the only relief I was getting from being swaddled head to mid-arm to knee in what felt like plastic, I didn't even fuss at her. Flap away, kid, flap away! So be warned, cooler climate, windy day? sure. One of those ladies who always needs a jacket and long sleeves? enjoy! Run warm or live in satan's armpit? give it a pass.

2. This thing just isn't waterproof.

Now, for the setup? I wore it straight from the package - no washing, no fooling around with it, just opened the zip pouch and put it on.
The weather in question? It wasn't a heavy rain or even blowing, just a miserable on again and off again drizzling - the sort of thing you'd get wet with if you stayed out a half hour or so in plain clothing. The temperature: Mid 70s F and not a breath of wind. The duration: a 20-30 minute walk with a fifteen minute period mid-point spent standing underneath a ceiling/out of the rain but still wearing the poncho.

All that said, I have twins under two who ride in a wagon style stroller and a 5 year old who has to walk a little under 3 blocks to get to her school - so I needed a poncho or rain coat. I can hardly hold an umbrella and push a stroller and run herd on a kid who likes to wander, so waterproof, something I would not need to fidget with or adjust once I had it on and lightweight enough to fit into a diaper pack. Cute was a slight bonus but not important. I was so excited to find this thing online after shelling out a few dollars every other week in rainy season to pick up gas station plastic ponchos like the ones you'd buy at a theme park - my kid always managed to tear them or they'd get caught on some zipper or brake lever on the stroller. So fabric was a plus. Washable was a plus. Staying dry was the priority.

This thing told me nope to the staying dry part.

So...drizzly, sporadic rain, no wind, and a quick walk with a 20 minute round trip, maybe. When I got back inside and took off the poncho, I realized everywhere it had rested in contact with my clothing was damp. I had assumed I was just sweaty, because as mentioned this thing is hot to wear, but my armpits were dry, the small of my back was dry, no swampy panties or the like - just the top of my shoulders, the area above my shoulder-blades, the top of my chest and the outside of my biceps. I'd been wearing layers - a cami beneath a tee. Cami - dry. Tee - damp in those places. Gross.

I examined the poncho, couldn't find any obvious leaking or places where the seams might not have been sealed - nothing that screamed out "damaged". I'm going to keep it in the stroller's storage as an emergency piece but no way would I recommend or buy this again.

제목: Decent umbrella, but customer service is outstanding! - UPDATED
본문:
I like to write my reviews well after having owned the product long enough to have an educated opinion of the product. We have had this umbrella for a year now. Early on it worked exactly as we wanted. But as mentioned by a few folks in previous reviews, you don't want to have it up in strong winds. We went to use it this summer and found that the main horizontal pole that attaches to the top of the umbrella spire had a plastic connector break. It is the main part that connects the umbrella to the horizontal extension pole, AND is responsible for the majority of the horizontal stability of the umbrella. I am quite surprised this part was made of plastic. While we did not try to use it in winds at all, I believe that over the course of time, and with normal breezes, this part just weakened and eventually broke. The only other knock on the product is that the dark blue canvas lost a LOT of its color and faded. You can tell from parts that are not exposed to the sun vs. those parts that are. Vast difference in color. These are the only negatives that we had for the umbrella. Yes, the piece breaking is a deal breaker, but it worked fine until that broke.

The positives from this purchase are that the customer service from WIKI is absolutely outstanding. Not only were we refunded the cost, but they readily accept input from their customers for product improvement. They are already working on an upgraded fabric to be more resistant to UV light. They also took some input regarding the part that broke. IMO, at a minimum, it should be metal like the rest of the umbrella framework, especially considering this particular part is so critical for umbrella stability.

I would definitely purchase from WIKI in the future knowing the upside of their customer service (which can be VERY lacking in today's times). If they upgrade the fabric, and fabricate that critical part with metal instead of plastic, I would give it another go and buy the umbrella again.
-------------------------------------------------------------------
UPDATE 1-12-22: Wiki has been in contact with me for the duration of our issue. And they have gone above and beyond in today's world of customer service. They have taken the recommendations/suggestions that myself, and others, had noted previously and made upgrades accordingly to their 2021 model. They have asked me to try a new umbrella and asked me to offer an updated review based on the improvements they have made, and I accepted. As a result, I am upping my review to 4 stars (from 3) not only for the exceptional Customer Service we have experienced in working with Wiki, but also the fact that they seem to care enough about their customers that they would not only accept recommendations, but act on them as well. Looking forward to the new version. I will update here again after we use it for a while to see how the improvements hold up!

This is an okay t-shirt that is made well from good materials, yet was made to look like a raggedy shirt. It's a shame- the material is 100% cotton and extremely soft. My final con on this shirt is the size. While it's true to size in the length, this is a very baggy shirt. While I didn't expect this to be a slim fit, it fit my husband more like a baggy medium than a regular small. If it weren't for the length, I would recommend sizing down. This also may not be a great fitting shirt on someone who is tall due to this problem as well.

Overall, this could be a well constructed shirt if it weren't for the fact that it was designed to look raggedy and worn out. Additionally, the sizing is off- too wide to fit as expected, yet too short to go a size down.

We live in Northern Wisconsin, where it is below freezing six months out of the year. Heavy duty snow gear is a requirement here. And while these boots are really nice, I'm a little perturbed that they are calling them "snow" boots. They are rain boots, plain and simple. Granted they lined them with extra fleece.... but they're still rainboots. True snow boots are designed with insulation to keep toes warm, where these rain boots are not. A layer of fleece is equivalent to putting on a second layer of socks, in my opinion. And rain boots (even with two layers of socks) are not enough protection for long stents of outdoor play in the snow.
With that said, they could still be useful boots in the dead of winter. Maybe in warmer states below us. Or for running errands -or- for short walks to school in freezing cold climates. And they're fantastic boots for the fall and spring months (when it's cold, just not ice cold). These boots are nice quality and should certainly last. But I was expecting snow boots and so I would have returned these. It's hard to recommend something I would have knowingly returned.

The zipper on these bags are also low quality, I used a bag a few times (less than 10 openings) and when I went to open the bag, the zipper just completely detached from the plastic bag itself so there's just no way to close it again.
